rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's nineteen builder trees go (a row of corals, jacarandas and ficus along the back fences, three jacarandas 3 m from the house fronts, a few in the yards inside the wrought-iron fence); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the swing set, the adirondack chair, on the open lot corner, and in yards 6-14 m from the houses.

trees.why: the back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the south-west yard with the white adirondack chair (2.4 m off): a ficus to sit under
the open lot corner inside the wrought-iron fence, 30 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the yard north of it, 12 m from the house, 31 m from the magnolia
the middle yard inside the same fence, 13.6 m from the house
the west back yard of the north row, 5.5 m from the house: the one tree of the old back fence row (one every 6 m)
